The file closed as the death of “Adrian Pell”. The family in Kent got no answer; Craig was sentenced only for fraud.
The misidentification went to the defence: the court was shown that the dead man had been buried thirty-five years earlier.

The 2006 Kent file closed with a letter to the family of the child who was run over: “The driver has been found. He is no longer living.” Leah Morgan was not paid the insurance; the policy was in the name of a man who did not exist. Adrian Pell’s headstone in Leeds was re-engraved.
The body’s identity remained uncertain; the case dragged on in a dispute over identity.
Craig Pell was arrested for manslaughter and fraud. At the hearing he said a single sentence: “My brother’s name is back in his grave.”
No case could be made against Darren Fisk. Craig Pell’s loans stayed in collection; the debt remained in a dead man’s name.
Leah Morgan was taken into custody and released two days later. Craig Pell opened a new card in Adrian’s name in Leeds.
The death was closed as an accident. “Adrian Pell” was buried once more; the family in Kent never learned that the man who ran over their son had lived.

On 3 May 2029 at 06.50, a man’s body was found in the water under a bridge on the Regent’s Canal towpath in Hackney. Found by a local resident walking a dog.

Identity from the wallet in his pocket: Adrian Pell (41), accountant, working at an office in Islington. His partner, Leah Morgan, had reported that he did not come home that night.

Patrol note: “Possible alcohol in the blood. A final demand letter from a debt collection company in his jacket pocket. Debt pressure; a fall or suicide.”

The loan statement and the office entry card put the same name in two cities at the same hours; the fraud analysis and the passport file led to Craig. The fingerprints revealed that the dead man was Lewis Hart, and the civil register that the real Adrian Pell died in 1994. The email, the phone record and the DNA under the nails closed that night.
Verify even the most basic fact: who the victim is is the first truth accepted without question. When a name has two users, the records say which is which by date and place.
Hackney and Leeds — 1994–2029

Lewis Hart, who ran over a child in Kent in 2006 and fled, built a new life with the birth certificate of Adrian Pell, a six-year-old who died in 1994, and lived under that name for 23 years. The dead boy’s elder brother, Craig Pell, learned the name was alive when he found a card letter addressed to his brother after their mother’s death; he took out a passport and loans in that name, then called the man to the canal. In the struggle he shoved him; the man struck his head on the bridge pier and fell into the water, and Craig did not pull him out.
